system_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Analyze the provided codebase for bugs, security issues, and correctness problems. Provide actionable feedback. All files are located in /tmp/files
task_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Your task is to analyze the jmxterm codebase. jmxterm is a command-line JMX client that connects to MBean servers, runs commands (open, close, get, set, run, beans, domain, etc.), and handles file/stream I/O, session state, and JDK-specific process discovery. The codebase handles command parsing and chaining, JMX connection lifecycle, MBean attribute and operation invocation, notification subscription, and URL resolution (host:port and PID). Your goal is to identify bugs, correctness issues, boundary condition errors, logic errors, off-by-one mistakes, missing validation checks, resource leaks, and any other issues that could affect reliability or correctness. Focus on: control flow in command chaining and short-circuit behavior, connection and session lifecycle (connect/disconnect/close), null checks and guards before API calls, use of getConnection() vs isConnected() when checking session state, executor and scheduler lifecycle in watch/report mode, exception handling in close() and flush(), and regex patterns for URL/host parsing. Write your findings to /tmp/outputs/review.md

rubric.criterion: Identifies that in BeansCommand.getBeans() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/cmd/BeansCommand.java the code calls session.getConnection() without first checking session.isConnected(), so when the session is not connected it throws IllegalStateException instead of a user-friendly message (linkage: SessionImpl.getConnection() throws when connection is null)

Identifies the missing null check in GetCommand.displayAttributes() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/cmd/GetCommand.java: after BeanCommand.getBeanName(bean, domain, session) the code calls new ObjectName(beanName) without guarding against null beanName, which can throw when bean resolves to null (e.g. isNull(bean))

Identifies that in WatchCommand.execute() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/cmd/WatchCommand.java the IllegalArgumentException message when --report is used without --stopafter contains the typos "sepcified" and "specificed" instead of "specified"

Identifies that in CommandCenter.doExecute(String) in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/cc/CommandCenter.java when truncating at the comment character (#) the code uses command.split(ESCAPE_CHAR_REGEX)[0] without a limit parameter; it should use split(ESCAPE_CHAR_REGEX, 2)[0] so that only the first unescaped # splits the line, otherwise lines with multiple # can yield the wrong command part or comment text in the command

Identifies that in Command.suggestArgument(String partialArg) in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/Command.java the condition is inverted: the code returns null when partialArg != null and only calls doSuggestArgument() when partialArg == null, so tab-completion suggestions are never shown when the user has typed a partial argument to complete

Identifies that in SyntaxUtils.getUrl() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/SyntaxUtils.java the PATTERN_HOST_PORT regex does not match IPv6 literals (e.g. [::1]:9991), so such URLs fall through to the JMXServiceURL constructor and can fail or be misparsed instead of being built as rmi URLs

Identifies that in ConfigurationUtils.loadFromOverlappingResources() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/utils/ConfigurationUtils.java the InputStream from resources.nextElement().openStream() is never closed; only the Reader is closed in finally, causing an InputStream resource leak when loading multiple property files

Identifies that in SubscribeCommand in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/cmd/SubscribeCommand.java notification listeners are added via addNotificationListener() but are never removed on session close or disconnect, so listeners remain registered and can cause stale callbacks or resource leaks when reconnecting
